items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: I play good and I’m getting hired by Woody Herman’s band, and I’m good for a while

ctx.x: If Eastman — I don’t know how many jazz majors graduate from Eastman every year, but if you multiply that times the number of universities in the country now who are doing similar work, what’s the prospect for a young talented musician with a degree, in the business?

Not too good, to be honest. And I think about that. Because I think not only in music but even say you have a degree in painting. Where are you going to go? You know, you have a degree in poetry. What are you going to do? You know, Starbucks? Hey. But I do believe that with passion and commitment and energy, those people, the ones that are that dedicated, will rise to someplace where they can do their art and make a living. It’s a difficult thing because there isn’t too much of a place in our society, and with…
think it’s necessary now for musicians to find creative ways to make a living and still stay true to their art.
